Tax Refund Guide for Korea Tourists 2026

How to claim your VAT tax refund in South Korea: minimum purchases, eligible stores, immediate refund in Myeongdong, and airport refund process.

⏱ 5 min read · 🇰🇷 Seoul, Korea · Updated 2026

Get Up to 10% Back on Your Shopping

South Korea charges a 10% VAT (Value Added Tax) on most goods. As a foreign tourist, you're legally entitled to claim this back on qualifying purchases. In Myeongdong, Gangnam, or COEX, a serious shopping trip could yield a refund of ₩50,000–₩300,000 or more. It's free money — don't leave it behind.

Who Qualifies?

  • Non-Korean residents visiting on a tourist visa
  • Foreign residents who have been in Korea less than 6 months
  • You must take the purchased goods out of Korea unused and unopened (cosmetics: sealed packaging)

Minimum Purchase Amount

Minimum spend at a single store: ₩30,000 (approximately $22 USD). No maximum. The more you spend, the bigger the refund.

Method 1: Immediate Refund (Best)

Many stores in Myeongdong, Dongdaemun, and Insadong offer 즉시환급 (immediate refund). You get your tax money back right at the store counter — no airport process needed.

  1. Look for the "즉시환급" or "Tax Free" sticker at the store entrance
  2. Show your passport at checkout
  3. Receive the refund in cash or as a discount on your bill

The refund is slightly less than the full 10% (around 7–8%) due to a small service fee.

💡 Myeongdong tip: Almost every K-beauty store, clothing shop, and department store on the main street participates in immediate refund. Always ask if you don't see the sticker.

Method 2: Airport Refund at Incheon

If you shopped at stores without immediate refund, claim at Incheon Airport:

  1. Before check-in: Go to Customs Stamp Desk. If refund amount exceeds ₩75,000, you must show the goods for inspection.
  2. After security (departure gates): Find Global Blue, KTIS, or Easy Tax Refund counters
  3. Present your passport, receipts, and stamped refund vouchers
  4. Choose cash (KRW, USD, EUR) or credit card refund

Method 3: Digital Refund (KTP App)

Korea has a growing digital refund system. Some stores are connected to the KTP (Korea Tax-free Platform) — your refund is credited to your credit card automatically within 2–4 weeks. No paper vouchers needed. Ask stores if they support "전자환급 (electronic refund)".

Best Shopping Areas for Tax Refunds

  • Myeongdong — Almost universal participation. Immediate refund available everywhere.
  • COEX Mall (Gangnam) — Electronics, luxury, department stores
  • Dongdaemun Design Plaza — Fashion, sportswear, streetwear
  • Insadong — Traditional crafts and souvenirs
  • Lotte/Shinsegae Duty Free — Tax already excluded at point of sale

Important Rules

  • Don't open or use items before leaving Korea (especially cosmetics)
  • Keep all receipts and tax refund vouchers organized
  • Refund vouchers expire — usually 3 months from purchase date
  • Minimum refund for airport processing: ₩30,000 per store, but you can combine across multiple stores
